## Student Loan Forgiveness in Louisiana [2026]: PSLF, IDR, and State Programs
Source: https://studentloanforgive.org/states/louisiana.html

← studentloanforgive.org home

Student Loan Forgiveness in Louisiana [2026]: PSLF, IDR, and State Programs

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Louisiana residents.

Forgiveness Paths for Louisiana Borrowers

Most federal student loan debt held by Louisiana residents is discharged through forgiveness programs, not bankruptcy. The four primary federal paths are Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), IDR long-term forgiveness (20-25 years), Teacher Loan Forgiveness, and Total and Permanent Disability discharge.

State-level programs add targeted relief on top of federal programs, especially for healthcare professionals, teachers in shortage areas, and public-sector employees.

PSLF in Louisiana

Moderate PSLF density: state government, LSU, Ochsner affiliates (nonprofit portions), VA.

Public Service Loan Forgiveness (20 U.S.C. Section 1087e(m)) discharges the remaining balance on Direct Loans after 120 qualifying monthly payments while working full-time for a qualifying employer - federal, state, tribal, or local government, or a 501(c)(3) public charity (EIN 41-5159631).

Louisiana PSLF requirements:

Qualifying employment - Full-time (30+ hours/week on average) at a qualifying employer. Louisiana public-school teachers, state-agency employees, federal-facility staff, and most nonprofit hospital workers qualify.

Qualifying loans - Direct Loans only. FFEL and Perkins borrowers must consolidate into a Direct Consolidation Loan first (this resets the 120-payment count unless under a time-limited waiver).

Qualifying payments - 120 on-time payments under an income-driven plan (SAVE, PAYE, IBR, ICR) or the 10-year Standard plan. Payments don't have to be consecutive.

Certification - Submit the PSLF Employment Certification Form annually (or when changing employers). This is the single highest-leverage administrative step for Louisiana PSLF candidates.

IDR and SAVE in Louisiana

SAVE plan; below-median LA income supports low IDR.

Income-Driven Repayment plans base the monthly payment on discretionary income (AGI minus 150-225% of federal poverty guidelines, depending on plan and family size). After 20-25 years of qualifying payments, remaining balance is forgiven.

PlanMonthly PaymentForgivenessLouisiana Availability

SAVE (formerly REPAYE)5-10% of discretionary (225% poverty threshold)20-25 yearsAvailable; current status subject to federal rulemaking

PAYE10% of discretionary (150% poverty threshold)20 yearsAvailable for borrowers with loans before Oct 2007

IBR (new borrowers post-2014)10% of discretionary20 yearsAvailable

IBR (older borrowers)15% of discretionary25 yearsAvailable

ICR20% of discretionary, or 12-year fixed, whichever less25 yearsAvailable; only ICR supports Parent PLUS after consolidation

Post-IDR-forgiveness tax treatment: the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) temporarily exempts forgiven student-debt amounts from federal taxable income through 2025; check current-year Treasury guidance for Louisiana filers.

Louisiana State-Specific Forgiveness Programs

Louisiana SREB State Doctoral Scholars; LA Nurse Faculty Loan Repayment.

State-level programs typically target professionals willing to serve in shortage areas. Key design features to check for any Louisiana program:

Service commitment - usually 2-5 years in a designated location.

Annual award - typically $10,000-$50,000/year, paid directly to the loan servicer.

Tax treatment - some states exempt the forgiven amount from state tax even when federal tax applies.

Stackability with PSLF - in most cases, state loan repayment awards stack with PSLF payments because PSLF only requires you make qualifying payments, not that you personally pay them.

See state-program inventory (if available) for detailed terms.

Total and Permanent Disability Discharge

Separate from forgiveness, TPD discharge (20 U.S.C. Section 1087(a)(2)) fully discharges federal Direct, FFEL, and Perkins loans for borrowers with a qualifying disability. Three paths:

VA determination - Service-connected disability rated 100% or Individual Unemployability.

SSA determination - SSDI or SSI with a 5-7 year review-cycle indicator.

Physician certification - MD or DO certifies a medical impairment preventing substantial gainful activity.

Post-2023 regulatory changes eliminated the 3-year income-monitoring post-TPD for most cases. ARPA also exempts TPD-discharged amounts from federal tax income through 2025. Check Louisiana-specific tax treatment separately.

Qualifying Employer Types in Louisiana

For PSLF and state programs, qualifying Louisiana employers fall into these categories:

Federal - VA, SSA, Dept. of Defense facilities, IHS, USPS, federal courts, and all executive-branch agencies with Louisiana offices.

State - Louisiana government agencies, state universities, state community colleges, state-funded clinics.

Local - county/municipal governments, public school districts, county hospitals, public health departments.

Tribal - federally recognized tribal governments and tribal health corporations.

Nonprofit (501(c)(3)) - hospitals, universities, museums, legal-aid organizations, community development corporations.

Employer eligibility can be verified at the Federal Student Aid PSLF Help Tool. Error rate on employer certifications has fallen substantially since 2021 reforms. See qualifying employer guide.

When Forgiveness Is Not Enough - Bankruptcy Path

Some Louisiana borrowers cannot wait 10-25 years for forgiveness: health, age, private-loan exposure, or total debt load makes bankruptcy more realistic. For those borrowers:

Section 523(a)(8) adversary - Undue hardship discharge. See Louisiana Brunner test application.

Private loans - Often dischargeable under McDaniel v. Navient reasoning without proving undue hardship.

Chapter 13 + IDR - A Louisiana debtor can use a 3-5 year Chapter 13 plan while simultaneously pursuing IDR/PSLF, then file an adversary after plan completion (strongest good-faith posture).

See Louisiana default consequences if already in default.

IDR plans

TPD discharge

Teacher loan forgiveness

Borrower defense

State programs

Louisiana Brunner test

Louisiana default

Employer eligibility can be verified at the Federal Student Aid PSLF Help Tool. Error rate on employer certifications has fallen substantially since 2021 reforms. See qualifying employer guide.

Michigan Federal Bankruptcy Data

Forgiveness is the preferred path for most Michigan borrowers with federal loans - but a significant subset still needs bankruptcy. These Michigan numbers show how often bankruptcy is the actual route.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,133 bankruptcy cases from Michigan's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 7633100.0%0.0%

Chapter 1350048.3%51.0%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Forgiveness Is Not Enough - Bankruptcy Path

Some Michigan borrowers cannot wait 10-25 years for forgiveness: health, age, private-loan exposure, or total debt load makes bankruptcy more realistic. For those borrowers:

Section 523(a)(8) adversary - Undue hardship discharge. See Michigan Brunner test application.

Private loans - Often dischargeable under McDaniel v. Navient reasoning without proving undue hardship.

Chapter 13 + IDR - A Michigan debtor can use a 3-5 year Chapter 13 plan while simultaneously pursuing IDR/PSLF, then file an adversary after plan completion (strongest good-faith posture).

See Michigan default consequences if already in default.

## Student Loan Forgiveness in Minnesota [2026]: PSLF, IDR, and State Programs
Source: https://studentloanforgive.org/states/minnesota.html

← studentloanforgive.org home

Student Loan Forgiveness in Minnesota [2026]: PSLF, IDR, and State Programs

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Minnesota residents.

Forgiveness Paths for Minnesota Borrowers

Most federal student loan debt held by Minnesota residents is discharged through forgiveness programs, not bankruptcy. The four primary federal paths are Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), IDR long-term forgiveness (20-25 years), Teacher Loan Forgiveness, and Total and Permanent Disability discharge.

State-level programs add targeted relief on top of federal programs, especially for healthcare professionals, teachers in shortage areas, and public-sector employees.

PSLF in Minnesota

High PSLF density: state agencies, UMN system, HealthPartners, nonprofit systems.

Public Service Loan Forgiveness (20 U.S.C. Section 1087e(m)) discharges the remaining balance on Direct Loans after 120 qualifying monthly payments while working full-time for a qualifying employer - federal, state, tribal, or local government, or a 501(c)(3) public charity (EIN 41-5159631).

Minnesota PSLF requirements:

Qualifying employment - Full-time (30+ hours/week on average) at a qualifying employer. Minnesota public-school teachers, state-agency employees, federal-facility staff, and most nonprofit hospital workers qualify.

Qualifying loans - Direct Loans only. FFEL and Perkins borrowers must consolidate into a Direct Consolidation Loan first (this resets the 120-payment count unless under a time-limited waiver).

Qualifying payments - 120 on-time payments under an income-driven plan (SAVE, PAYE, IBR, ICR) or the 10-year Standard plan. Payments don't have to be consecutive.

Certification - Submit the PSLF Employment Certification Form annually (or when changing employers). This is the single highest-leverage administrative step for Minnesota PSLF candidates.

IDR and SAVE in Minnesota

SAVE plan; MN median income near national, COL varies by metro.

Income-Driven Repayment plans base the monthly payment on discretionary income (AGI minus 150-225% of federal poverty guidelines, depending on plan and family size). After 20-25 years of qualifying payments, remaining balance is forgiven.

PlanMonthly PaymentForgivenessMinnesota Availability

SAVE (formerly REPAYE)5-10% of discretionary (225% poverty threshold)20-25 yearsAvailable; current status subject to federal rulemaking

PAYE10% of discretionary (150% poverty threshold)20 yearsAvailable for borrowers with loans before Oct 2007

IBR (new borrowers post-2014)10% of discretionary20 yearsAvailable

IBR (older borrowers)15% of discretionary25 yearsAvailable

ICR20% of discretionary, or 12-year fixed, whichever less25 yearsAvailable; only ICR supports Parent PLUS after consolidation

Post-IDR-forgiveness tax treatment: the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) temporarily exempts forgiven student-debt amounts from federal taxable income through 2025; check current-year Treasury guidance for Minnesota filers.

Minnesota State-Specific Forgiveness Programs

MN Loan Repayment Program (multi-profession); MN Urban Teacher Grant.

State-level programs typically target professionals willing to serve in shortage areas. Key design features to check for any Minnesota program:

Service commitment - usually 2-5 years in a designated location.

Annual award - typically $10,000-$50,000/year, paid directly to the loan servicer.

Tax treatment - some states exempt the forgiven amount from state tax even when federal tax applies.

Stackability with PSLF - in most cases, state loan repayment awards stack with PSLF payments because PSLF only requires you make qualifying payments, not that you personally pay them.

See state-program inventory (if available) for detailed terms.

Total and Permanent Disability Discharge

Separate from forgiveness, TPD discharge (20 U.S.C. Section 1087(a)(2)) fully discharges federal Direct, FFEL, and Perkins loans for borrowers with a qualifying disability. Three paths:

VA determination - Service-connected disability rated 100% or Individual Unemployability.

SSA determination - SSDI or SSI with a 5-7 year review-cycle indicator.

Physician certification - MD or DO certifies a medical impairment preventing substantial gainful activity.

Post-2023 regulatory changes eliminated the 3-year income-monitoring post-TPD for most cases. ARPA also exempts TPD-discharged amounts from federal tax income through 2025. Check Minnesota-specific tax treatment separately.

Qualifying Employer Types in Minnesota

For PSLF and state programs, qualifying Minnesota employers fall into these categories:

Federal - VA, SSA, Dept. of Defense facilities, IHS, USPS, federal courts, and all executive-branch agencies with Minnesota offices.

State - Minnesota government agencies, state universities, state community colleges, state-funded clinics.

Local - county/municipal governments, public school districts, county hospitals, public health departments.

Tribal - federally recognized tribal governments and tribal health corporations.

Nonprofit (501(c)(3)) - hospitals, universities, museums, legal-aid organizations, community development corporations.

Employer eligibility can be verified at the Federal Student Aid PSLF Help Tool. Error rate on employer certifications has fallen substantially since 2021 reforms. See qualifying employer guide.

Minnesota Federal Bankruptcy Data

Forgiveness is the preferred path for most Minnesota borrowers with federal loans - but a significant subset still needs bankruptcy. These Minnesota numbers show how often bankruptcy is the actual route.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 395 bankruptcy cases from Minnesota's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 737999.7%0.3%

Chapter 1316n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Forgiveness Is Not Enough - Bankruptcy Path

Some Minnesota borrowers cannot wait 10-25 years for forgiveness: health, age, private-loan exposure, or total debt load makes bankruptcy more realistic. For those borrowers:

Section 523(a)(8) adversary - Undue hardship discharge. See Minnesota Brunner test application.

Private loans - Often dischargeable under McDaniel v. Navient reasoning without proving undue hardship.

Chapter 13 + IDR - A Minnesota debtor can use a 3-5 year Chapter 13 plan while simultaneously pursuing IDR/PSLF, then file an adversary after plan completion (strongest good-faith posture).

See Minnesota default consequences if already in default.

IBR (new borrowers post-2014)10% of discretionary20 yearsAvailable

IBR (older borrowers)15% of discretionary25 yearsAvailable

ICR20% of discretionary, or 12-year fixed, whichever less25 yearsAvailable; only ICR supports Parent PLUS after consolidation

Post-IDR-forgiveness tax treatment: the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) temporarily exempts forgiven student-debt amounts from federal taxable income through 2025; check current-year Treasury guidance for Nebraska filers.

Nebraska State-Specific Forgiveness Programs

NE Rural Health Advisory loan repayment; NE State Loan Repayment.

State-level programs typically target professionals willing to serve in shortage areas. Key design features to check for any Nebraska program:

Service commitment - usually 2-5 years in a designated location.

Annual award - typically $10,000-$50,000/year, paid directly to the loan servicer.

Tax treatment - some states exempt the forgiven amount from state tax even when federal tax applies.

Stackability with PSLF - in most cases, state loan repayment awards stack with PSLF payments because PSLF only requires you make qualifying payments, not that you personally pay them.

See state-program inventory (if available) for detailed terms.

Total and Permanent Disability Discharge

Separate from forgiveness, TPD discharge (20 U.S.C. Section 1087(a)(2)) fully discharges federal Direct, FFEL, and Perkins loans for borrowers with a qualifying disability. Three paths:

VA determination - Service-connected disability rated 100% or Individual Unemployability.

SSA determination - SSDI or SSI with a 5-7 year review-cycle indicator.

Physician certification - MD or DO certifies a medical impairment preventing substantial gainful activity.

Post-2023 regulatory changes eliminated the 3-year income-monitoring post-TPD for most cases. ARPA also exempts TPD-discharged amounts from federal tax income through 2025. Check Nebraska-specific tax treatment separately.

Qualifying Employer Types in Nebraska

For PSLF and state programs, qualifying Nebraska employers fall into these categories:

Federal - VA, SSA, Dept. of Defense facilities, IHS, USPS, federal courts, and all executive-branch agencies with Nebraska offices.

State - Nebraska government agencies, state universities, state community colleges, state-funded clinics.

Local - county/municipal governments, public school districts, county hospitals, public health departments.

Tribal - federally recognized tribal governments and tribal health corporations.

Nonprofit (501(c)(3)) - hospitals, universities, museums, legal-aid organizations, community development corporations.

Employer eligibility can be verified at the Federal Student Aid PSLF Help Tool. Error rate on employer certifications has fallen substantially since 2021 reforms. See qualifying employer guide.

Nebraska Federal Bankruptcy Data

Forgiveness is the preferred path for most Nebraska borrowers with federal loans - but a significant subset still needs bankruptcy. These Nebraska numbers show how often bankruptcy is the actual route.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 75 bankruptcy cases from Nebraska's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 757100.0%0.0%

Chapter 1318n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Forgiveness Is Not Enough - Bankruptcy Path

Some Nebraska borrowers cannot wait 10-25 years for forgiveness: health, age, private-loan exposure, or total debt load makes bankruptcy more realistic. For those borrowers:

Section 523(a)(8) adversary - Undue hardship discharge. See Nebraska Brunner test application.

Private loans - Often dischargeable under McDaniel v. Navient reasoning without proving undue hardship.

Chapter 13 + IDR - A Nebraska debtor can use a 3-5 year Chapter 13 plan while simultaneously pursuing IDR/PSLF, then file an adversary after plan completion (strongest good-faith posture).

See Nebraska default consequences if already in default.

## Student Loan Forgiveness in Nevada [2026]: PSLF, IDR, and State Programs
Source: https://studentloanforgive.org/states/nevada.html

← studentloanforgive.org home

Student Loan Forgiveness in Nevada [2026]: PSLF, IDR, and State Programs

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Nevada residents.

Forgiveness Paths for Nevada Borrowers

Most federal student loan debt held by Nevada residents is discharged through forgiveness programs, not bankruptcy. The four primary federal paths are Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), IDR long-term forgiveness (20-25 years), Teacher Loan Forgiveness, and Total and Permanent Disability discharge.

State-level programs add targeted relief on top of federal programs, especially for healthcare professionals, teachers in shortage areas, and public-sector employees.

PSLF in Nevada

Moderate PSLF density: state agencies, UNLV/UNR, Clark County schools.

Public Service Loan Forgiveness (20 U.S.C. Section 1087e(m)) discharges the remaining balance on Direct Loans after 120 qualifying monthly payments while working full-time for a qualifying employer - federal, state, tribal, or local government, or a 501(c)(3) public charity (EIN 41-5159631).

Nevada PSLF requirements:

Qualifying employment - Full-time (30+ hours/week on average) at a qualifying employer. Nevada public-school teachers, state-agency employees, federal-facility staff, and most nonprofit hospital workers qualify.

Qualifying loans - Direct Loans only. FFEL and Perkins borrowers must consolidate into a Direct Consolidation Loan first (this resets the 120-payment count unless under a time-limited waiver).

Qualifying payments - 120 on-time payments under an income-driven plan (SAVE, PAYE, IBR, ICR) or the 10-year Standard plan. Payments don't have to be consecutive.

Certification - Submit the PSLF Employment Certification Form annually (or when changing employers). This is the single highest-leverage administrative step for Nevada PSLF candidates.

IDR and SAVE in Nevada

SAVE plan; Las Vegas COL offset.

Income-Driven Repayment plans base the monthly payment on discretionary income (AGI minus 150-225% of federal poverty guidelines, depending on plan and family size). After 20-25 years of qualifying payments, remaining balance is forgiven.

PlanMonthly PaymentForgivenessNevada Availability

SAVE (formerly REPAYE)5-10% of discretionary (225% poverty threshold)20-25 yearsAvailable; current status subject to federal rulemaking

PAYE10% of discretionary (150% poverty threshold)20 yearsAvailable for borrowers with loans before Oct 2007

IBR (new borrowers post-2014)10% of discretionary20 yearsAvailable

IBR (older borrowers)15% of discretionary25 yearsAvailable

ICR20% of discretionary, or 12-year fixed, whichever less25 yearsAvailable; only ICR supports Parent PLUS after consolidation

Post-IDR-forgiveness tax treatment: the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) temporarily exempts forgiven student-debt amounts from federal taxable income through 2025; check current-year Treasury guidance for Nevada filers.

Nevada State-Specific Forgiveness Programs

NV Health Service Corps; NV State Nursing Loan Repayment.

State-level programs typically target professionals willing to serve in shortage areas. Key design features to check for any Nevada program:

Service commitment - usually 2-5 years in a designated location.

Annual award - typically $10,000-$50,000/year, paid directly to the loan servicer.

Tax treatment - some states exempt the forgiven amount from state tax even when federal tax applies.

Stackability with PSLF - in most cases, state loan repayment awards stack with PSLF payments because PSLF only requires you make qualifying payments, not that you personally pay them.

See state-program inventory (if available) for detailed terms.

Total and Permanent Disability Discharge

Separate from forgiveness, TPD discharge (20 U.S.C. Section 1087(a)(2)) fully discharges federal Direct, FFEL, and Perkins loans for borrowers with a qualifying disability. Three paths:

VA determination - Service-connected disability rated 100% or Individual Unemployability.

SSA determination - SSDI or SSI with a 5-7 year review-cycle indicator.

Physician certification - MD or DO certifies a medical impairment preventing substantial gainful activity.

Post-2023 regulatory changes eliminated the 3-year income-monitoring post-TPD for most cases. ARPA also exempts TPD-discharged amounts from federal tax income through 2025. Check Nevada-specific tax treatment separately.

Qualifying Employer Types in Nevada

For PSLF and state programs, qualifying Nevada employers fall into these categories:

Federal - VA, SSA, Dept. of Defense facilities, IHS, USPS, federal courts, and all executive-branch agencies with Nevada offices.

State - Nevada government agencies, state universities, state community colleges, state-funded clinics.

Local - county/municipal governments, public school districts, county hospitals, public health departments.

Tribal - federally recognized tribal governments and tribal health corporations.

Nonprofit (501(c)(3)) - hospitals, universities, museums, legal-aid organizations, community development corporations.

Employer eligibility can be verified at the Federal Student Aid PSLF Help Tool. Error rate on employer certifications has fallen substantially since 2021 reforms. See qualifying employer guide.

Nevada Federal Bankruptcy Data

Forgiveness is the preferred path for most Nevada borrowers with federal loans - but a significant subset still needs bankruptcy. These Nevada numbers show how often bankruptcy is the actual route.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 242 bankruptcy cases from Nevada's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 716493.4%5.9%

Chapter 137837.2%62.8%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Forgiveness Is Not Enough - Bankruptcy Path

Some Nevada borrowers cannot wait 10-25 years for forgiveness: health, age, private-loan exposure, or total debt load makes bankruptcy more realistic. For those borrowers:

Section 523(a)(8) adversary - Undue hardship discharge. See Nevada Brunner test application.

Private loans - Often dischargeable under McDaniel v. Navient reasoning without proving undue hardship.

Chapter 13 + IDR - A Nevada debtor can use a 3-5 year Chapter 13 plan while simultaneously pursuing IDR/PSLF, then file an adversary after plan completion (strongest good-faith posture).

See Nevada default consequences if already in default.

Source: https://studentloanforgive.org/states/new-york.html

← studentloanforgive.org home

Student Loan Forgiveness in New York [2026]: PSLF, IDR, and State Programs

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for New York residents.

Forgiveness Paths for New York Borrowers

Most federal student loan debt held by New York residents is discharged through forgiveness programs, not bankruptcy. The four primary federal paths are Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), IDR long-term forgiveness (20-25 years), Teacher Loan Forgiveness, and Total and Permanent Disability discharge.

State-level programs add targeted relief on top of federal programs, especially for healthcare professionals, teachers in shortage areas, and public-sector employees.

PSLF in New York

Very high PSLF density: CUNY/SUNY, state agencies, NYC government, massive nonprofit healthcare.

Public Service Loan Forgiveness (20 U.S.C. Section 1087e(m)) discharges the remaining balance on Direct Loans after 120 qualifying monthly payments while working full-time for a qualifying employer - federal, state, tribal, or local government, or a 501(c)(3) public charity (EIN 41-5159631).

New York PSLF requirements:

Qualifying employment - Full-time (30+ hours/week on average) at a qualifying employer. New York public-school teachers, state-agency employees, federal-facility staff, and most nonprofit hospital workers qualify.

Qualifying loans - Direct Loans only. FFEL and Perkins borrowers must consolidate into a Direct Consolidation Loan first (this resets the 120-payment count unless under a time-limited waiver).

Qualifying payments - 120 on-time payments under an income-driven plan (SAVE, PAYE, IBR, ICR) or the 10-year Standard plan. Payments don't have to be consecutive.

Certification - Submit the PSLF Employment Certification Form annually (or when changing employers). This is the single highest-leverage administrative step for New York PSLF candidates.

IDR and SAVE in New York

SAVE plan; NYC COL offset high in IDR modeling.

Income-Driven Repayment plans base the monthly payment on discretionary income (AGI minus 150-225% of federal poverty guidelines, depending on plan and family size). After 20-25 years of qualifying payments, remaining balance is forgiven.

PlanMonthly PaymentForgivenessNew York Availability

SAVE (formerly REPAYE)5-10% of discretionary (225% poverty threshold)20-25 yearsAvailable; current status subject to federal rulemaking

PAYE10% of discretionary (150% poverty threshold)20 yearsAvailable for borrowers with loans before Oct 2007

IBR (new borrowers post-2014)10% of discretionary20 yearsAvailable

IBR (older borrowers)15% of discretionary25 yearsAvailable

ICR20% of discretionary, or 12-year fixed, whichever less25 yearsAvailable; only ICR supports Parent PLUS after consolidation

Post-IDR-forgiveness tax treatment: the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) temporarily exempts forgiven student-debt amounts from federal taxable income through 2025; check current-year Treasury guidance for New York filers.

New York State-Specific Forgiveness Programs

NY State Teacher Loan Forgiveness Program; NY STAR; Licensed Social Worker Loan Forgiveness; Nurses Across NY.

State-level programs typically target professionals willing to serve in shortage areas. Key design features to check for any New York program:

Service commitment - usually 2-5 years in a designated location.

Annual award - typically $10,000-$50,000/year, paid directly to the loan servicer.

Tax treatment - some states exempt the forgiven amount from state tax even when federal tax applies.

Stackability with PSLF - in most cases, state loan repayment awards stack with PSLF payments because PSLF only requires you make qualifying payments, not that you personally pay them.

See state-program inventory (if available) for detailed terms.

Total and Permanent Disability Discharge

Separate from forgiveness, TPD discharge (20 U.S.C. Section 1087(a)(2)) fully discharges federal Direct, FFEL, and Perkins loans for borrowers with a qualifying disability. Three paths:

VA determination - Service-connected disability rated 100% or Individual Unemployability.

SSA determination - SSDI or SSI with a 5-7 year review-cycle indicator.

Physician certification - MD or DO certifies a medical impairment preventing substantial gainful activity.

Post-2023 regulatory changes eliminated the 3-year income-monitoring post-TPD for most cases. ARPA also exempts TPD-discharged amounts from federal tax income through 2025. Check New York-specific tax treatment separately.

Qualifying Employer Types in New York

For PSLF and state programs, qualifying New York employers fall into these categories:

Federal - VA, SSA, Dept. of Defense facilities, IHS, USPS, federal courts, and all executive-branch agencies with New York offices.

State - New York government agencies, state universities, state community colleges, state-funded clinics.

Local - county/municipal governments, public school districts, county hospitals, public health departments.

Tribal - federally recognized tribal governments and tribal health corporations.

Nonprofit (501(c)(3)) - hospitals, universities, museums, legal-aid organizations, community development corporations.

Employer eligibility can be verified at the Federal Student Aid PSLF Help Tool. Error rate on employer certifications has fallen substantially since 2021 reforms. See qualifying employer guide.

New York Federal Bankruptcy Data

Forgiveness is the preferred path for most New York borrowers with federal loans - but a significant subset still needs bankruptcy. These New York numbers show how often bankruptcy is the actual route.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,231 bankruptcy cases from New York's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 71,14598.7%1.2%

Chapter 138628.2%71.8%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Forgiveness Is Not Enough - Bankruptcy Path

Some New York borrowers cannot wait 10-25 years for forgiveness: health, age, private-loan exposure, or total debt load makes bankruptcy more realistic. For those borrowers:

Section 523(a)(8) adversary - Undue hardship discharge. See New York Brunner test application.

Private loans - Often dischargeable under McDaniel v. Navient reasoning without proving undue hardship.

Chapter 13 + IDR - A New York debtor can use a 3-5 year Chapter 13 plan while simultaneously pursuing IDR/PSLF, then file an adversary after plan completion (strongest good-faith posture).

See New York default consequences if already in default.

IDR plans

TPD discharge

Teacher loan forgiveness

Borrower defense

State programs

New York Brunner test

New York default

## Student Loan Forgiveness in Ohio [2026]: PSLF, IDR, and State Programs

Student Loan Forgiveness in Ohio [2026]: PSLF, IDR, and State Programs

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Ohio residents.

Forgiveness Paths for Ohio Borrowers

Qualifying Employer Types in Oklahoma

For PSLF and state programs, qualifying Oklahoma employers fall into these categories:

Federal - VA, SSA, Dept. of Defense facilities, IHS, USPS, federal courts, and all executive-branch agencies with Oklahoma offices.

State - Oklahoma government agencies, state universities, state community colleges, state-funded clinics.

Local - county/municipal governments, public school districts, county hospitals, public health departments.

Tribal - federally recognized tribal governments and tribal health corporations.

Nonprofit (501(c)(3)) - hospitals, universities, museums, legal-aid organizations, community development corporations.

Employer eligibility can be verified at the Federal Student Aid PSLF Help Tool. Error rate on employer certifications has fallen substantially since 2021 reforms. See qualifying employer guide.

Oklahoma Federal Bankruptcy Data

Forgiveness is the preferred path for most Oklahoma borrowers with federal loans - but a significant subset still needs bankruptcy. These Oklahoma numbers show how often bankruptcy is the actual route.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 112 bankruptcy cases from Oklahoma's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 711099.1%0.9%

Chapter 132n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Forgiveness Is Not Enough - Bankruptcy Path

Some Oklahoma borrowers cannot wait 10-25 years for forgiveness: health, age, private-loan exposure, or total debt load makes bankruptcy more realistic. For those borrowers:

Section 523(a)(8) adversary - Undue hardship discharge. See Oklahoma Brunner test application.

Private loans - Often dischargeable under McDaniel v. Navient reasoning without proving undue hardship.

Chapter 13 + IDR - A Oklahoma debtor can use a 3-5 year Chapter 13 plan while simultaneously pursuing IDR/PSLF, then file an adversary after plan completion (strongest good-faith posture).

See Oklahoma default consequences if already in default.

## Student Loan Forgiveness in Oregon [2026]: PSLF, IDR, and State Programs
Source: https://studentloanforgive.org/states/oregon.html

← studentloanforgive.org home

Student Loan Forgiveness in Oregon [2026]: PSLF, IDR, and State Programs

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Oregon residents.

Forgiveness Paths for Oregon Borrowers

Most federal student loan debt held by Oregon residents is discharged through forgiveness programs, not bankruptcy. The four primary federal paths are Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), IDR long-term forgiveness (20-25 years), Teacher Loan Forgiveness, and Total and Permanent Disability discharge.

State-level programs add targeted relief on top of federal programs, especially for healthcare professionals, teachers in shortage areas, and public-sector employees.

PSLF in Oregon

High PSLF density: state agencies, OHSU, OR public schools.

Public Service Loan Forgiveness (20 U.S.C. Section 1087e(m)) discharges the remaining balance on Direct Loans after 120 qualifying monthly payments while working full-time for a qualifying employer - federal, state, tribal, or local government, or a 501(c)(3) public charity (EIN 41-5159631).

Oregon PSLF requirements:

Qualifying employment - Full-time (30+ hours/week on average) at a qualifying employer. Oregon public-school teachers, state-agency employees, federal-facility staff, and most nonprofit hospital workers qualify.

Qualifying loans - Direct Loans only. FFEL and Perkins borrowers must consolidate into a Direct Consolidation Loan first (this resets the 120-payment count unless under a time-limited waiver).

Qualifying payments - 120 on-time payments under an income-driven plan (SAVE, PAYE, IBR, ICR) or the 10-year Standard plan. Payments don't have to be consecutive.

Certification - Submit the PSLF Employment Certification Form annually (or when changing employers). This is the single highest-leverage administrative step for Oregon PSLF candidates.

IDR and SAVE in Oregon

SAVE plan; 9th Cir. Pena gloss on Brunner complements PSLF path.

Income-Driven Repayment plans base the monthly payment on discretionary income (AGI minus 150-225% of federal poverty guidelines, depending on plan and family size). After 20-25 years of qualifying payments, remaining balance is forgiven.

PlanMonthly PaymentForgivenessOregon Availability

SAVE (formerly REPAYE)5-10% of discretionary (225% poverty threshold)20-25 yearsAvailable; current status subject to federal rulemaking

PAYE10% of discretionary (150% poverty threshold)20 yearsAvailable for borrowers with loans before Oct 2007

IBR (new borrowers post-2014)10% of discretionary20 yearsAvailable

IBR (older borrowers)15% of discretionary25 yearsAvailable

ICR20% of discretionary, or 12-year fixed, whichever less25 yearsAvailable; only ICR supports Parent PLUS after consolidation

Post-IDR-forgiveness tax treatment: the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) temporarily exempts forgiven student-debt amounts from federal taxable income through 2025; check current-year Treasury guidance for Oregon filers.

Oregon State-Specific Forgiveness Programs

Scholars for a Healthy Oregon; OR Rural Medical Practitioner Insurance Subsidy.

State-level programs typically target professionals willing to serve in shortage areas. Key design features to check for any Oregon program:

Service commitment - usually 2-5 years in a designated location.

Annual award - typically $10,000-$50,000/year, paid directly to the loan servicer.

Tax treatment - some states exempt the forgiven amount from state tax even when federal tax applies.

Stackability with PSLF - in most cases, state loan repayment awards stack with PSLF payments because PSLF only requires you make qualifying payments, not that you personally pay them.

See state-program inventory (if available) for detailed terms.

Total and Permanent Disability Discharge

Separate from forgiveness, TPD discharge (20 U.S.C. Section 1087(a)(2)) fully discharges federal Direct, FFEL, and Perkins loans for borrowers with a qualifying disability. Three paths:

VA determination - Service-connected disability rated 100% or Individual Unemployability.

SSA determination - SSDI or SSI with a 5-7 year review-cycle indicator.

Physician certification - MD or DO certifies a medical impairment preventing substantial gainful activity.

Post-2023 regulatory changes eliminated the 3-year income-monitoring post-TPD for most cases. ARPA also exempts TPD-discharged amounts from federal tax income through 2025. Check Oregon-specific tax treatment separately.

Qualifying Employer Types in Oregon

For PSLF and state programs, qualifying Oregon employers fall into these categories:

Federal - VA, SSA, Dept. of Defense facilities, IHS, USPS, federal courts, and all executive-branch agencies with Oregon offices.

State - Oregon government agencies, state universities, state community colleges, state-funded clinics.

Local - county/municipal governments, public school districts, county hospitals, public health departments.

Tribal - federally recognized tribal governments and tribal health corporations.

Nonprofit (501(c)(3)) - hospitals, universities, museums, legal-aid organizations, community development corporations.

Employer eligibility can be verified at the Federal Student Aid PSLF Help Tool. Error rate on employer certifications has fallen substantially since 2021 reforms. See qualifying employer guide.

When Forgiveness Is Not Enough - Bankruptcy Path

Some Oregon borrowers cannot wait 10-25 years for forgiveness: health, age, private-loan exposure, or total debt load makes bankruptcy more realistic. For those borrowers:

Section 523(a)(8) adversary - Undue hardship discharge. See Oregon Brunner test application.

Private loans - Often dischargeable under McDaniel v. Navient reasoning without proving undue hardship.

Chapter 13 + IDR - A Oregon debtor can use a 3-5 year Chapter 13 plan while simultaneously pursuing IDR/PSLF, then file an adversary after plan completion (strongest good-faith posture).

See Oregon default consequences if already in default.

IDR and SAVE in South Dakota

SAVE plan; 8th Cir. totality favorable for hardship cases.

Income-Driven Repayment plans base the monthly payment on discretionary income (AGI minus 150-225% of federal poverty guidelines, depending on plan and family size). After 20-25 years of qualifying payments, remaining balance is forgiven.

PlanMonthly PaymentForgivenessSouth Dakota Availability

SAVE (formerly REPAYE)5-10% of discretionary (225% poverty threshold)20-25 yearsAvailable; current status subject to federal rulemaking

PAYE10% of discretionary (150% poverty threshold)20 yearsAvailable for borrowers with loans before Oct 2007

IBR (new borrowers post-2014)10% of discretionary20 yearsAvailable

IBR (older borrowers)15% of discretionary25 yearsAvailable

ICR20% of discretionary, or 12-year fixed, whichever less25 yearsAvailable; only ICR supports Parent PLUS after consolidation

Post-IDR-forgiveness tax treatment: the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) temporarily exempts forgiven student-debt amounts from federal taxable income through 2025; check current-year Treasury guidance for South Dakota filers.

South Dakota State-Specific Forgiveness Programs

SD Recruitment Assistance Program.

State-level programs typically target professionals willing to serve in shortage areas. Key design features to check for any South Dakota program:

Service commitment - usually 2-5 years in a designated location.

Annual award - typically $10,000-$50,000/year, paid directly to the loan servicer.

Tax treatment - some states exempt the forgiven amount from state tax even when federal tax applies.

Stackability with PSLF - in most cases, state loan repayment awards stack with PSLF payments because PSLF only requires you make qualifying payments, not that you personally pay them.

See state-program inventory (if available) for detailed terms.

Total and Permanent Disability Discharge

Separate from forgiveness, TPD discharge (20 U.S.C. Section 1087(a)(2)) fully discharges federal Direct, FFEL, and Perkins loans for borrowers with a qualifying disability. Three paths:

VA determination - Service-connected disability rated 100% or Individual Unemployability.

SSA determination - SSDI or SSI with a 5-7 year review-cycle indicator.

Physician certification - MD or DO certifies a medical impairment preventing substantial gainful activity.

Post-2023 regulatory changes eliminated the 3-year income-monitoring post-TPD for most cases. ARPA also exempts TPD-discharged amounts from federal tax income through 2025. Check South Dakota-specific tax treatment separately.

Qualifying Employer Types in South Dakota

For PSLF and state programs, qualifying South Dakota employers fall into these categories:

Federal - VA, SSA, Dept. of Defense facilities, IHS, USPS, federal courts, and all executive-branch agencies with South Dakota offices.

State - South Dakota government agencies, state universities, state community colleges, state-funded clinics.

Local - county/municipal governments, public school districts, county hospitals, public health departments.

Tribal - federally recognized tribal governments and tribal health corporations.

Nonprofit (501(c)(3)) - hospitals, universities, museums, legal-aid organizations, community development corporations.

Employer eligibility can be verified at the Federal Student Aid PSLF Help Tool. Error rate on employer certifications has fallen substantially since 2021 reforms. See qualifying employer guide.

When Forgiveness Is Not Enough - Bankruptcy Path

Some South Dakota borrowers cannot wait 10-25 years for forgiveness: health, age, private-loan exposure, or total debt load makes bankruptcy more realistic. For those borrowers:

Section 523(a)(8) adversary - Undue hardship discharge. See South Dakota Brunner test application.

Private loans - Often dischargeable under McDaniel v. Navient reasoning without proving undue hardship.

Chapter 13 + IDR - A South Dakota debtor can use a 3-5 year Chapter 13 plan while simultaneously pursuing IDR/PSLF, then file an adversary after plan completion (strongest good-faith posture).

See South Dakota default consequences if already in default.

IDR plans

TPD discharge

Borrower defense

State programs

## Student Loan Forgiveness in Tennessee [2026]: PSLF, IDR, and State Programs
Source: https://studentloanforgive.org/states/tennessee.html

← studentloanforgive.org home

Student Loan Forgiveness in Tennessee [2026]: PSLF, IDR, and State Programs

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Tennessee residents.

Forgiveness Paths for Tennessee Borrowers

Most federal student loan debt held by Tennessee residents is discharged through forgiveness programs, not bankruptcy. The four primary federal paths are Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), IDR long-term forgiveness (20-25 years), Teacher Loan Forgiveness, and Total and Permanent Disability discharge.

State-level programs add targeted relief on top of federal programs, especially for healthcare professionals, teachers in shortage areas, and public-sector employees.

PSLF in Tennessee

Moderate-high PSLF density: state agencies, Vanderbilt (nonprofit portions), state universities.

Public Service Loan Forgiveness (20 U.S.C. Section 1087e(m)) discharges the remaining balance on Direct Loans after 120 qualifying monthly payments while working full-time for a qualifying employer - federal, state, tribal, or local government, or a 501(c)(3) public charity (EIN 41-5159631).

Tennessee PSLF requirements:

Qualifying employment - Full-time (30+ hours/week on average) at a qualifying employer. Tennessee public-school teachers, state-agency employees, federal-facility staff, and most nonprofit hospital workers qualify.

Qualifying loans - Direct Loans only. FFEL and Perkins borrowers must consolidate into a Direct Consolidation Loan first (this resets the 120-payment count unless under a time-limited waiver).

Qualifying payments - 120 on-time payments under an income-driven plan (SAVE, PAYE, IBR, ICR) or the 10-year Standard plan. Payments don't have to be consecutive.

Certification - Submit the PSLF Employment Certification Form annually (or when changing employers). This is the single highest-leverage administrative step for Tennessee PSLF candidates.

IDR and SAVE in Tennessee

SAVE plan; high Ch 13 volume means PSLF stability valuable.

Income-Driven Repayment plans base the monthly payment on discretionary income (AGI minus 150-225% of federal poverty guidelines, depending on plan and family size). After 20-25 years of qualifying payments, remaining balance is forgiven.

PlanMonthly PaymentForgivenessTennessee Availability

SAVE (formerly REPAYE)5-10% of discretionary (225% poverty threshold)20-25 yearsAvailable; current status subject to federal rulemaking

PAYE10% of discretionary (150% poverty threshold)20 yearsAvailable for borrowers with loans before Oct 2007

IBR (new borrowers post-2014)10% of discretionary20 yearsAvailable

IBR (older borrowers)15% of discretionary25 yearsAvailable

ICR20% of discretionary, or 12-year fixed, whichever less25 yearsAvailable; only ICR supports Parent PLUS after consolidation

Post-IDR-forgiveness tax treatment: the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) temporarily exempts forgiven student-debt amounts from federal taxable income through 2025; check current-year Treasury guidance for Tennessee filers.

TN State Loan Repayment Program (TSLRP); TN Teacher Loan Forgiveness Program.

State-level programs typically target professionals willing to serve in shortage areas. Key design features to check for any Tennessee program:

Service commitment - usually 2-5 years in a designated location.

Annual award - typically $10,000-$50,000/year, paid directly to the loan servicer.

Tax treatment - some states exempt the forgiven amount from state tax even when federal tax applies.

Stackability with PSLF - in most cases, state loan repayment awards stack with PSLF payments because PSLF only requires you make qualifying payments, not that you personally pay them.

See state-program inventory (if available) for detailed terms.

Post-2023 regulatory changes eliminated the 3-year income-monitoring post-TPD for most cases. ARPA also exempts TPD-discharged amounts from federal tax income through 2025. Check Tennessee-specific tax treatment separately.

Qualifying Employer Types in Tennessee

Federal - VA, SSA, Dept. of Defense facilities, IHS, USPS, federal courts, and all executive-branch agencies with Tennessee offices.

State - Tennessee government agencies, state universities, state community colleges, state-funded clinics.

Local - county/municipal governments, public school districts, county hospitals, public health departments.

Tribal - federally recognized tribal governments and tribal health corporations.

Nonprofit (501(c)(3)) - hospitals, universities, museums, legal-aid organizations, community development corporations.

Employer eligibility can be verified at the Federal Student Aid PSLF Help Tool. Error rate on employer certifications has fallen substantially since 2021 reforms. See qualifying employer guide.

Tennessee Federal Bankruptcy Data

Forgiveness is the preferred path for most Tennessee borrowers with federal loans - but a significant subset still needs bankruptcy. These Tennessee numbers show how often bankruptcy is the actual route.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,840 bankruptcy cases from Tennessee's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 758995.5%4.5%

Chapter 131,25117.3%82.7%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Forgiveness Is Not Enough - Bankruptcy Path

Some Tennessee borrowers cannot wait 10-25 years for forgiveness: health, age, private-loan exposure, or total debt load makes bankruptcy more realistic. For those borrowers:

Section 523(a)(8) adversary - Undue hardship discharge. See Tennessee Brunner test application.

Private loans - Often dischargeable under McDaniel v. Navient reasoning without proving undue hardship.

Chapter 13 + IDR - A Tennessee debtor can use a 3-5 year Chapter 13 plan while simultaneously pursuing IDR/PSLF, then file an adversary after plan completion (strongest good-faith posture).

Student Loan Forgiveness in Virginia [2026]: PSLF, IDR, and State Programs

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Virginia residents.

Forgiveness Paths for Virginia Borrowers

Most federal student loan debt held by Virginia residents is discharged through forgiveness programs, not bankruptcy. The four primary federal paths are Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), IDR long-term forgiveness (20-25 years), Teacher Loan Forgiveness, and Total and Permanent Disability discharge.

State-level programs add targeted relief on top of federal programs, especially for healthcare professionals, teachers in shortage areas, and public-sector employees.

PSLF in Virginia

Very high PSLF density: federal agencies (Pentagon, Langley, Quantico), state government, state university systems.

Public Service Loan Forgiveness (20 U.S.C. Section 1087e(m)) discharges the remaining balance on Direct Loans after 120 qualifying monthly payments while working full-time for a qualifying employer - federal, state, tribal, or local government, or a 501(c)(3) public charity (EIN 41-5159631).

Virginia PSLF requirements:

Qualifying employment - Full-time (30+ hours/week on average) at a qualifying employer. Virginia public-school teachers, state-agency employees, federal-facility staff, and most nonprofit hospital workers qualify.

Qualifying loans - Direct Loans only. FFEL and Perkins borrowers must consolidate into a Direct Consolidation Loan first (this resets the 120-payment count unless under a time-limited waiver).

Qualifying payments - 120 on-time payments under an income-driven plan (SAVE, PAYE, IBR, ICR) or the 10-year Standard plan. Payments don't have to be consecutive.

Certification - Submit the PSLF Employment Certification Form annually (or when changing employers). This is the single highest-leverage administrative step for Virginia PSLF candidates.

IDR and SAVE in Virginia

SAVE plan; high NOVA COL offset.

Income-Driven Repayment plans base the monthly payment on discretionary income (AGI minus 150-225% of federal poverty guidelines, depending on plan and family size). After 20-25 years of qualifying payments, remaining balance is forgiven.

PlanMonthly PaymentForgivenessVirginia Availability

SAVE (formerly REPAYE)5-10% of discretionary (225% poverty threshold)20-25 yearsAvailable; current status subject to federal rulemaking

PAYE10% of discretionary (150% poverty threshold)20 yearsAvailable for borrowers with loans before Oct 2007

IBR (new borrowers post-2014)10% of discretionary20 yearsAvailable

IBR (older borrowers)15% of discretionary25 yearsAvailable

ICR20% of discretionary, or 12-year fixed, whichever less25 yearsAvailable; only ICR supports Parent PLUS after consolidation

Post-IDR-forgiveness tax treatment: the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) temporarily exempts forgiven student-debt amounts from federal taxable income through 2025; check current-year Treasury guidance for Virginia filers.

Virginia State-Specific Forgiveness Programs

VA State Loan Repayment Program; VA Nurse Educator Loan Forgiveness.

State-level programs typically target professionals willing to serve in shortage areas. Key design features to check for any Virginia program:

Service commitment - usually 2-5 years in a designated location.

Annual award - typically $10,000-$50,000/year, paid directly to the loan servicer.

Tax treatment - some states exempt the forgiven amount from state tax even when federal tax applies.

Stackability with PSLF - in most cases, state loan repayment awards stack with PSLF payments because PSLF only requires you make qualifying payments, not that you personally pay them.

See state-program inventory (if available) for detailed terms.

Total and Permanent Disability Discharge

Separate from forgiveness, TPD discharge (20 U.S.C. Section 1087(a)(2)) fully discharges federal Direct, FFEL, and Perkins loans for borrowers with a qualifying disability. Three paths:

VA determination - Service-connected disability rated 100% or Individual Unemployability.

SSA determination - SSDI or SSI with a 5-7 year review-cycle indicator.

Physician certification - MD or DO certifies a medical impairment preventing substantial gainful activity.

Post-2023 regulatory changes eliminated the 3-year income-monitoring post-TPD for most cases. ARPA also exempts TPD-discharged amounts from federal tax income through 2025. Check Virginia-specific tax treatment separately.

Qualifying Employer Types in Virginia

For PSLF and state programs, qualifying Virginia employers fall into these categories:

Federal - VA, SSA, Dept. of Defense facilities, IHS, USPS, federal courts, and all executive-branch agencies with Virginia offices.

State - Virginia government agencies, state universities, state community colleges, state-funded clinics.

Local - county/municipal governments, public school districts, county hospitals, public health departments.

Tribal - federally recognized tribal governments and tribal health corporations.

Nonprofit (501(c)(3)) - hospitals, universities, museums, legal-aid organizations, community development corporations.

Employer eligibility can be verified at the Federal Student Aid PSLF Help Tool. Error rate on employer certifications has fallen substantially since 2021 reforms. See qualifying employer guide.

Virginia Federal Bankruptcy Data

Forgiveness is the preferred path for most Virginia borrowers with federal loans - but a significant subset still needs bankruptcy. These Virginia numbers show how often bankruptcy is the actual route.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,064 bankruptcy cases from Virginia's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 7514n/an/a

Chapter 1355071.2%28.7%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Forgiveness Is Not Enough - Bankruptcy Path

Some Virginia borrowers cannot wait 10-25 years for forgiveness: health, age, private-loan exposure, or total debt load makes bankruptcy more realistic. For those borrowers:

Section 523(a)(8) adversary - Undue hardship discharge. See Virginia Brunner test application.

Private loans - Often dischargeable under McDaniel v. Navient reasoning without proving undue hardship.

Chapter 13 + IDR - A Virginia debtor can use a 3-5 year Chapter 13 plan while simultaneously pursuing IDR/PSLF, then file an adversary after plan completion (strongest good-faith posture).

See Virginia default consequences if already in default.

TPD discharge

Teacher loan forgiveness

Borrower defense

State programs

Virginia Brunner test

State - Wyoming government agencies, state universities, state community colleges, state-funded clinics.

Local - county/municipal governments, public school districts, county hospitals, public health departments.

Tribal - federally recognized tribal governments and tribal health corporations.

Nonprofit (501(c)(3)) - hospitals, universities, museums, legal-aid organizations, community development corporations.

Employer eligibility can be verified at the Federal Student Aid PSLF Help Tool. Error rate on employer certifications has fallen substantially since 2021 reforms. See qualifying employer guide.

When Forgiveness Is Not Enough - Bankruptcy Path

Some Wyoming borrowers cannot wait 10-25 years for forgiveness: health, age, private-loan exposure, or total debt load makes bankruptcy more realistic. For those borrowers:

Section 523(a)(8) adversary - Undue hardship discharge. See Wyoming Brunner test application.

Private loans - Often dischargeable under McDaniel v. Navient reasoning without proving undue hardship.

Chapter 13 + IDR - A Wyoming debtor can use a 3-5 year Chapter 13 plan while simultaneously pursuing IDR/PSLF, then file an adversary after plan completion (strongest good-faith posture).

See Wyoming default consequences if already in default.

### How does Public Service Loan Forgiveness work? - Student Loan Forgiveness Guide

Home › Common Questions › How does Public Service Loan Forgiveness work?

People Also Ask

How does Public Service Loan Forgiveness work?

PSLF forgives the remaining balance on Direct Loans after you make 120 qualifying monthly payments (10 years) while working full-time for a qualifying employer - government agencies, 501(c)(3) nonprofits, or certain other public service organizations. The forgiven amount is tax-free.

Public Service Loan Forgiveness is one of the most valuable student loan programs available, but it requires careful compliance with specific requirements.

Eligibility Requirements

Loan type: Must be Direct Loans (FFEL and Perkins loans can be consolidated into Direct Loans to qualify)

Repayment plan: Must be on a qualifying repayment plan: an income-driven plan, the Repayment Assistance Plan, or the 10-year Standard plan (which qualifies but leaves little or nothing to forgive)

Employer: Federal, state, local, or tribal government, or 501(c)(3) nonprofit

Employment: Full-time (30+ hours/week or employer's definition of full-time)

Payments: 120 qualifying payments (do not need to be consecutive)

The Application Process

Submit the PSLF Form annually or whenever you change employers. After 120 qualifying payments, submit the final application. Use the PSLF Help Tool at StudentAid.gov/pslf; the Department of Education reviews your employment and payment history.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Not submitting the Employment Certification Form annually (makes it harder to verify at the end)

Being on the wrong repayment plan (standard 10-year plan qualifies but leaves nothing to forgive)

Having FFEL loans that need to be consolidated first

Pausing payments unnecessarily (forbearance months do not count)

Federal Student Aid publishes current PSLF approval counts and dollar totals in its FSA Data Center at StudentAid.gov/data-center.

Common Questions

Clear, data-backed answers to the most frequently asked questions

Understanding Your Bankruptcy Options

Bankruptcy law provides several paths to financial relief, each designed for different situations. Chapter 7 offers a fresh start through liquidation of non-exempt assets and discharge of qualifying debts, typically completed in 3 to 6 months. Chapter 13 allows you to keep your property while repaying debts over 3 to 5 years. Chapter 11 provides reorganization options for businesses and high-debt individuals. Understanding which chapter fits your situation requires analyzing your income, assets, debts, and financial goals.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the different types of bankruptcy?

The most common types are Chapter 7 (liquidation for individuals and businesses), Chapter 13 (repayment plan for individuals with regular income), and Chapter 11 (reorganization for businesses). Each chapter has different eligibility requirements, timelines, and outcomes. A bankruptcy attorney or legal aid organization can help determine which option fits your situation.

How much does it cost to file bankruptcy?

Court filing fees are $338 for Chapter 7 and $313 for Chapter 13 as of 2026. Attorney fees vary by location and complexity but typically range from $1,000 to $2,500 for Chapter 7 and $2,500 to $5,000 for Chapter 13. Fee waivers are available for filers below 150% of the federal poverty guidelines.

Will bankruptcy stop creditor calls and lawsuits?

Yes. The automatic stay under 11 U.S.C. Section 362 takes effect immediately when you file and stops most collection activities, including phone calls, letters, lawsuits, wage garnishments, and foreclosure or repossession actions. Creditors who violate the stay can be held in contempt of court.

### Will my student loans be forgiven after 20 years? - Student Loan Forgiveness Guide
Source: https://studentloanforgive.org/paa/will-my-student-loans-be-forgiven-after-20-years.html

Skip to content

studentloanforgive.org

Home
Questions

Home › Common Questions › Will my student loans be forgiven after 20 years?

People Also Ask

Will my student loans be forgiven after 20 years?

Yes, if you are on an income-driven repayment plan. Under IBR, PAYE, and the SAVE plan, any remaining balance is forgiven after 20 years of payments for undergraduate loans, or 25 years for graduate loans. The forgiven amount is currently tax-free through 2025 under the American Rescue Plan Act.

Income-driven repayment (IDR) forgiveness is an automatic benefit for borrowers who make consistent payments on qualifying plans.

IDR Forgiveness Timelines

SAVE Plan: 20 years (undergraduate) or 25 years (graduate). Borrowers with original balances under $12,000 may qualify in as few as 10 years.

PAYE: 20 years for all loans

IBR (new borrowers after 7/1/2014): 20 years

IBR (older borrowers): 25 years

ICR: 25 years

Tax Implications

Under the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, student loan forgiveness is not treated as taxable income through December 31, 2025. After that date, forgiven amounts may be taxable as income unless Congress extends the provision. This is a major consideration for anyone expecting a large forgiveness amount.

IDR Account Adjustment

The Department of Education conducted a one-time account adjustment in 2023-2024 that credited borrowers with additional qualifying payments, including periods of forbearance and certain deferments. This adjustment moved many borrowers significantly closer to the 20/25-year forgiveness threshold.

If you are on an IDR plan, check your payment count through your servicer or studentaid.gov. You may be closer to forgiveness than you realize.
